correctness.rationale: The geometric fixed-locus orbit-barycenter lemma is proved with explicit inverse. The complete orbit graph is computed from all graph edges. If f>=1, a singleton-label vertex at level j has open neighborhood contained in that of each nonsingleton-orbit vertex there, giving a valid dominated-vertex strong collapse at every deletion; the result is exactly mu_ell(K_f). If f=0, all remaining orbit vertices at each level have identical open neighborhoods, and collapses leave P_(ell+1). The integral homotopy types follow from the standard path formula, an isolated vertex for f=1, and the cited Carnero Bravo Corollary 7 for f>=2. The standalone verifier confirmed 168 orbit graph cases, 462 domination reductions, and mod-2 homology on 110 bounded cases; the infinite proof does not depend on these computations.

value.rationale: The complete system of geometric fixed-space homotopy types under every subgroup is a natural equivariant datum and extends well beyond ordinary Betti numbers and elementwise character calculations. The exact strong-collapse theorem is a structural statement applying to all n, levels and subgroup orbit partitions; unexpectedly, all nontrivial label orbit sizes disappear and only the number of labels globally fixed by H remains. The cases f=0, f=1, and f>=2 exhibit different periodic sphere, contractible, and wedge patterns. It offers useful input to equivariant obstruction and fixed-point comparisons without claiming to determine all equivariant maps.
